name: HTU21D temperature & humidity sensor
description: TE Connectivity (MEAS) HTU21D(F) digital relative humidity (0–100 %, ±2 % typical) and temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.3 °C typical) sensor with an I2C interface at fixed address 0x40; the chip itself runs on 1.5–3.6 V. Sold as: GY-21 HTU21D temperature & humidity module (4-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA; on-board 3.3 V regulator and MOSFET level shifting, so VIN takes 3.3–5 V).
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Module supply, 3.3–5 V (on-board regulator feeds the chip 3.3 V)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (level-shifted, pull-up on the module)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (level-shifted, pull-up on the module)

supplierQuery: GY-21 HTU21D temperature humidity sensor module I2C
buildNotes: Power VIN from the same voltage as your board's logic (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico); the module's regulator and level shifters handle 5 V boards too.
No-hold measurement: write 0xF3 (temperature) or 0xF5 (humidity), wait at least 50 ms / 16 ms, then read 3 bytes: MSB, LSB (low 2 bits are status), CRC.
Check the CRC (poly 0x31, init 0x00) and clear the two status bits before converting: T = -46.85 + 175.72*S/65536, RH = -6 + 125*S/65536.
The address is fixed at 0x40 (shared with Si7021/SHT21/INA219 defaults), so only one per I2C bus without a multiplexer.
Keep the sensor away from the regulator and the microcontroller, which warm the air nearby.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from htu21d import HTU21D

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = HTU21D(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.1f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
